findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type, so anonymous and renderer checks collide
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey is built from namespace, subject UID, action, resource name, and folder, but not the identity type. Anonymous and renderer subjects both resolve to user UID "0" (for example anonymous:0 and render:0), and users and service accounts can also share a UID. A denial written for one principal is therefore returned for another principal on the same action/resource/folder. Concretely, an anonymous Check for dashboards:read/dash1 stores key org-12.perm_0_dashboards:read_dash1_, and a later renderer Check for the same dashboard hits that key and is denied without consulting renderer permissions, breaking rendering. Include the identity type (or full subject type) in the denial key.

findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous because fields are joined with underscores
findings.body: The denial key concatenates user UID, action, resource name, and parent folder with literal "_" separators. Grafana UIDs can contain underscores and resource name/folder are caller-controlled, so different tuples can produce the same key. For example, name "a_b" with parent "c" and name "a" with parent "b_c" both produce the same suffix. A denial cached for one resource would then deny an unrelated resource. Use length-prefixed or escaped components, or hash a structured key.

findings.title: Every distinct denied resource name causes a fresh permission DB query
findings.body: When cached identity permissions exist but do not allow the requested resource, Check falls through to getIdentityPermissions and queries the permission store. The denial cache only remembers the exact (action, name, parent) tuple, so callers can send checks for arbitrary distinct dashboard/folder UIDs (for example anonymous probes of /api/dashboards/uid/<random>) and force one permission DB query per UID. Previously these cache-hit checks were served without touching the DB. This is a DB-load/DoS regression; consider coalescing or marking a user/action as freshly queried rather than falling back per resource name.

findings.title: Tests seed the denial cache manually and never verify Check populates it
findings.body: The new denial-cache test manually calls permDenialCache.Set before invoking Check. There is no test that performs a Check returning false from the permission store and then asserts the denial is written, nor a test that a denial for one identity type does not affect another identity type. As a result, a regression where Check never writes denials, writes them under a mismatched key, or collides anonymous and renderer entries would pass the current test suite.
